category_title: Students who react with aggression or outbursts when losing or frustrated
minimal_context: The student is playing a board game involving rolling dice and moving pieces during a nurture group session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is your turn to roll the dice for the board game.

STUDENT: I have to win this. Winning is really important.

TUTOR: Go ahead and roll the dice to see what number you get.

STUDENT: (Rolls the dice) No! I am losing the game!

TUTOR: It is just a game, please move your piece.

STUDENT: I didn't roll the correct number! (Throws things across the table and stamps off)

options.A: Teach multiple peers in the nurture group strategies to engage the student in a game interaction by asking for help or asking if they want to play together.
options.B: Ask metacognitive questions about the purpose and value of the game (e.g., 'Why is what we just played important?' 'How will this help us to be better players?').
options.C: Implement a specific 'Termination' stage counting down the final three to five sessions of the nurture group program.
options.D: Implement daily activities focused on recognizing, understanding, and accepting a wide range of feelings; teaching the distinction between feeling and behaving.
